info.title: wwg API
info.description: The Wasatch Wargamers Campaign App API.

get.summary: Reports whether the API and its dependencies are healthy.

post.summary:
Ends a masquerade (decision 0012): back to the Admin's own session, without a password, if
the masquerade may still go on. 409 if the session isn't a masquerade.

get.summary:
Every unit in the campaign, sorted by army then name (every member): what the map draws
where it may (positions follow the visibility rule).

post.summary:
Adds library units to the army (Umpire or Admin), each as the campaign's own copy. Only
units from the army's factions (409), and none already in the campaign (409).

get.summary:
Places matching search (areas and settlements, not addresses), for the
Umpire to frame the map on (Umpire or Admin). 503 if the geocoding service fails.

An army's turns, newest first, with their orders and history (its commander, the Umpire and
Admins: the visibility rule).

Each of the army's units' forced marches as the open turn began, and the attrition moving
this turn would cost, as a multiple of the rules' scale (its commander, the Umpire and
Admins: they follow its moves).

The attrition the open turn's orders cost, for each unit that owes any (Umpire or Admin):
what starting the next turn asks them to confirm.

The campaign's depots the viewer may see, by army then name: the Umpire's and Admins', all;
a commander's, their own army's; anyone else's, none (they follow its moves).

post.summary: Places a depot for the army (Umpire or Admin), in a hex of the campaign's grid.

Starts the next turn (Umpire or Admin), once every army's turn in the open one is Completed
and every unit is on the map: the open turn closes and the next opens, a Draft for every
army. The attrition the closing turn cost is applied as the Umpire confirms it: a loss for
each unit that owes one (decision 0018). Every commander is emailed.

get.summary:
The campaign's turns and where each stands (every member). The Umpire sees every army's
turn, and what stops the campaign (or, once it's running, the next turn) starting; a
commander sees their own army's, and everyone the counts.

post.summary: Creates an account and signs it in.
Signs in with email and password. Repeated failures lock the account briefly.

Swaps the refresh cookie for a new access token and a new refresh cookie (sliding: the 30
days start again). Fails if the cookie is missing, unreadable or expired, or the account is
gone or its security stamp changed (password change, sign out everywhere). A masquerade
(decision 0012) goes on only while it may: see Task<AppUser?> TokenService.MasqueradingAdminAsync(Masquerade masquerade).

Signs out this browser by removing the refresh cookie. An access token already issued keeps
working until it expires (at most 30 minutes); the app discards it.

Emails a password reset link, if there's an account for the email. Always succeeds, so it
can't be used to find out which emails have accounts.

Sets a new password with the code from a reset link. This signs out every existing session
and clears any sign-in lockout.

get.summary: The signed-in user's profile.

put.summary: Updates the signed-in user's first and last name.

Changes the password (the current one is required). Every other session is signed out; the
response carries new tokens so this one keeps working.

Changes the email the account signs in with (the current password is required). Every other
session is signed out, a notice goes to the old address, and the response carries new
tokens so this session keeps working.

post.summary: Signs out every session, this one included: every access and refresh token stops working.

get.summary:
Users, sorted by last then first name, one page at a time. `search` matches any part of
the first name, last name or email, ignoring case.
One user's details.

delete.summary:
Deletes a user and their sign-in data; their sessions end immediately. Admins can't delete
their own account.

post.summary:
Starts a masquerade as the user (decision 0012): the session becomes theirs, with exactly
their permissions, marked as the Admin's masquerade and ending after
`Auth:MasqueradeLifetime`. Not as yourself, and not while already masquerading (409).

put.summary:
Makes a user a Manager, or not (decision 0015): they edit the library. It applies at once
(the library's access rule reads the role from the database).

get.summary:
Every campaign, sorted by name, one page at a time. `search` matches any part of the
name, ignoring case; `withoutUmpire` keeps only campaigns with no Umpire.

put.summary:
Makes a user the campaign's Umpire. A Player is promoted (and their army left unassigned);
anyone else joins as the Umpire.
The previous Umpire, if there is one, becomes a Player. Choosing the current Umpire changes
nothing.

get.summary: The campaigns the caller is in, with their role, sorted by name.

post.summary: Starts a campaign. The caller becomes its Umpire.

get.summary: A campaign's details: its Umpire (if it has one) and the caller's role.

put.summary: Changes the campaign's name and description (Umpire or Admin).

delete.summary:
Deletes the campaign and everything in it: its members, armies and units (Umpire or
Admin). The database's cascades do the rest.

get.summary: The campaign's current join code (Umpire or Admin).

post.summary:
Replaces the join code, so the old join link stops working (Umpire or Admin). Existing
members stay.

get.summary:
The campaign's members, with the army each Player commands: the Umpire first, then Players
by name.

delete.summary: Leaves the campaign (Players). The Umpire can't leave: an Admin sets a new Umpire instead.
Removes a Player from the campaign (Umpire or Admin).

get.summary: The campaign a join link is for: its name and Umpire. No sign-in needed.

post.summary:
Joins the campaign as a Player: 201. Already a member (including its Umpire): 200 with the
existing role, and nothing changes.

get.summary: The campaign's sides, sorted by name, with how many armies each has.

put.summary: Renames a side (Umpire or Admin). 409 if another has that name.

get.summary:
Every army in the campaign, with its commander, sorted by name. All members see them all,
unassigned ones included.

post.summary:
Adds an army, optionally with a commander, side and factions (Umpire or Admin). A campaign has at
most 8 armies (409). Without a colour it gets the first one no other army has.

get.summary:
An army's details and units. Every member sees every army's (read-only); where the units
are is a separate question (DESIGN.md §5.2, the visibility rule).

put.summary:
Changes an army's name, side, colour, nation and factions (Umpire or Admin). A faction the
army has units from can't be dropped (409).

delete.summary:
Deletes an army and its units (Umpire or Admin), while the campaign is setting up; after it
starts, that would erase their history (409).

put.summary:
Makes a Player the army's commander, replacing any other (Umpire or Admin). A Player
commands at most one army: 409 if they already command another.

delete.summary: Leaves the army without a commander (Umpire or Admin).

put.summary:
Changes the campaign's copy of a unit: name, type, Fighting Factor and points (Umpire or
Admin). The library unit stays as it is.

delete.summary:
Removes a unit from the army (Umpire or Admin), while the campaign is setting up; the
library unit stays.

get.summary:
The unit's points history once the campaign started, oldest first (every member, as they
see its points): each change, its turn, and why.

The campaign's map settings (every member): its bounds (null until set), label language,
distance unit, layers and hex size. Before the Umpire saves any, the defaults.

put.summary:
Changes the campaign's map settings (Umpire or Admin). Bounds run west to east and south to
north. The bounds and hex size lay out the grid: once the campaign has started they're
fixed (409); while setting up, changing them moves each placement to the new hex holding
the old one's centre (or takes it off the map if that's outside the new grid), and clears
the terrain, which belonged to the old hexes.

get.summary:
The campaign's terrain (every member): the hexes and edges with something on them. Empty
until inferred or set.

put.summary:
Saves the terrain inferred for the whole grid (Umpire or Admin): it replaces what inference
saved before, and the hexes and edges the Umpire set stay as they are. 409 without an area.

The Umpire sets a hex's terrain (Umpire or Admin); inference leaves it alone from then on.
404 for a hex outside the grid, 409 without an area.

The Umpire sets an edge's road, river and waterway (Umpire or Admin); inference leaves it alone from
then on. The edge is on hex (q, r)'s N, NE or SE side; 404 unless it touches the grid, 409
without an area.

get.summary:
The hexes' actual terrain the caller may see: the Umpire (or an Admin) all of it, with who
asked and who it's shown to; a member what's shown to their army, or to all.

post.summary:
The Umpire shakes the rule book's three dice for a hex (Umpire or Admin; p. 57): the red
die with its modifier from the hex's map terrain, the white, and the green if favourability
is wanted. A new roll replaces the hex's old one, keeping who it's shown to.

put.summary:
The Umpire sets a hex's actual terrain and who sees it (Umpire or Admin): changing a roll,
or setting one without dice. The dice, if any, are kept as they fell.

delete.summary: Forgets a hex's actual terrain (Umpire or Admin), and who it was shown to.

get.summary:
The campaign's calendar (every member): the first turn's day and time of day, and whose
infantry march further each Morning or less each Afternoon (the rule book's, until the
Umpire changes them).

put.summary:
Changes the campaign's calendar (Umpire or Admin). Its turns are relabelled, those played
too; the marches apply to orders given from now on.

get.summary:
The campaign's concentration settings (every member): the most points of infantry and of
cavalry a side may have in a hex, and the unit types counted towards each.

put.summary:
Changes the campaign's concentration settings (Umpire or Admin). A unit type counts towards
one limit at most; types in neither are free.

get.summary:
Where the campaign's units are, as the caller may see them (the visibility rule): the Umpire
every army's, a commander their own. Without turn, where they are now
(each unit's latest Completed turn); with a closed turn, where they were after it; with the
open one, their orders in it, whatever its status.

post.summary:
Starts the campaign (Umpire or Admin): turn 0 closes, with every army's placements as where
its units are, and turn 1 opens, a Draft for every army. 409 if it has started already, or
with what's stopping it (no area, no armies, an army without a side, units not placed).

put.summary:
Places a unit in a hex of the grid (Umpire or Admin): while setting up, in turn 0; once
started, a unit added since that has no position yet (it's placed where its army last was, in the
army's turn in the last closed campaign turn, which can't be reverted). Inside the
campaign's area, which must be set.

delete.summary: Takes a unit off the map again (Umpire or Admin), while setting up only.

get.summary:
The campaign's movement table (every member): hexes a turn for each class on each ground.
The rule book's until the Umpire changes it.

put.summary:
Replaces the campaign's movement table (Umpire or Admin): every class on each of its
grounds (land units on land, boats on water), once, 0 to 20 hexes a turn in halves. It
applies to orders given from now on.

delete.summary: Goes back to the rule book's movement table (Umpire or Admin).

put.summary:
Gives a unit its order for the turn: Move along a path of adjacent hexes from its current
one, inside the grid (and for the commander, one its movement class can afford this turn:
DESIGN.md §5.2); or Hold, where it is. Replaces any order it had. The army's commander gives orders while the turn is a
Draft in the open campaign turn; the Umpire and Admins while it's a Draft or Submitted, on
the commander's behalf (decision 0011), which goes in the turn's history.

delete.summary:
Takes back a unit's order for the turn: the army's commander while it's a Draft; the
Umpire and Admins while it's a Draft or Submitted, which goes in the turn's history.

put.summary: Moves, renames or changes a depot (Umpire or Admin).

delete.summary: Removes a depot (Umpire or Admin): it was captured, destroyed or given up.

post.summary:
Submits the army's turn for the Umpire to approve (the army's commander, or the Umpire or an
Admin on its behalf): a Draft in the open turn, once every unit on the map has an order.
Only the Umpire changes it while it's Submitted.

Approves a Submitted turn in the open turn (Umpire or Admin), once every unit on the map
has an order: it's Completed.

Sends a Submitted turn in the open turn back to its commander as a Draft (Umpire or
Admin), with a note on the turn and on units if wanted.

Reverts a Completed turn in the open turn to a Draft (Umpire or Admin), with a note on the
turn and on units if wanted. Turns in closed campaign turns can't be reverted.

get.summary: The library's factions, sorted by name, with how many units each has.

post.summary: Adds a faction to the library (Manager or Admin).

get.summary: A faction, with its units sorted by name.

put.summary: Renames a faction, or changes its flag (Manager or Admin).

delete.summary:
Deletes an empty faction (Manager or Admin). 409 while it has units, or an army takes units
from it.

post.summary: Adds a unit to a faction (Manager or Admin).

put.summary: Changes a library unit (Manager or Admin). Campaigns it's already in keep their copies.

delete.summary: Deletes a library unit (Manager or Admin). 409 while it's in a campaign.

unitIds.description: The library units: none already in the campaign.

AddArmyUnitsRequest.description: Adds library units to an army, from the factions it takes units from.

umpireName.description: The Umpire's name, or null if it has none.

AdminCampaignSummary.description: A campaign in the admin list of every campaign.

ArmyColor.description:
An army's colour on the map and beside its name: one of the front-end's 8 palette colours,
which it tunes for contrast in light and dark. Stored by name, so the palette can change.

ArmyFactionResponse.description: A library faction an army takes its units from.

oneOf.description: Its commander, or null if unassigned.

nation.description: The nation it fights for, drawn as its flag.

factions.description: The library factions it takes its units from, sorted by name.

ArmyResponse.description: An army's details, with its units.

ArmySide.description: The side an army is in.

oneOf.description: Its commander, or null if unassigned.

nation.description: The nation it fights for, drawn as its flag.

ArmySummary.description: An army in the campaign's army list. Every member sees every army.

id.description: The army turn's ID (orders are given through it).

open.description: Whether it's in the open campaign turn.

orders.description: Its units' orders, and so positions after it.

history.description: What happened to it, oldest first.

ArmyTurnDetails.description: An army's turn, with its orders and history.

byName.description: Who, or null if their account is gone.

note.description: The Umpire's note, when sending back or reverting.

ArmyTurnEventDto.description: One step in an army turn's history.

ArmyTurnEventKind.description: What happened to an army's turn.

ArmyTurnSummary.description: An army's part in a campaign turn.

unitId.description: The library unit it was copied from.

nation.description: The nation it marches as (step 45): its faction's, or its army's when the faction has none.

type.description: What kind of troops it is.

ArmyUnitResponse.description: A unit in an army: the campaign's copy of a library unit.

fightingFactor.description: Its Fighting Factor, which sets the rules' scale.

forcedMarchTurns.description: Its turns of forced march, this one included.

multiplier.description: This turn's multiple of the scale: 1, 2, 4…

loss.description: The whole points it loses (what it carries of a point adds in).

AttritionDueResponse.description: A unit's attrition for the open turn's orders, for the Umpire to confirm (decision 0018).

points.description: The points it loses (0 for none).

AttritionLossRequest.description: The Umpire's confirmed attrition for one unit.

startDate.description: The first turn's day, or null if not set.

firstTurnPart.description: The first turn's time of day.

morningNations.description: Whose infantry move a flat hex further each Morning.

afternoonNations.description: Whose infantry move a flat hex less each Afternoon.

rules.description: Whether the nations are the rule book's.

CampaignCalendarResponse.description: A campaign's calendar (step 45): when its turns fall, and whose infantry march faster or slower.

infantryTypes.description: The unit types counted towards the infantry limit.

cavalryTypes.description: The unit types counted towards the cavalry limit.

infantryLimit.description: The most points of infantry a side may have in a hex.

cavalryLimit.description: The most points of cavalry a side may have in a hex.

CampaignConcentrationResponse.description:
A campaign's concentration settings (step 46, decision 0017): the most points of infantry and
of cavalry a side may have in a hex, and the unit types counted towards each (the rest are free).

edges.description: The edges with roads or rivers.

CampaignGridResponse.description:
A campaign's terrain: the hexes and edges with something on them. Any other hex is Flat with
nothing on it, and any other edge has no road or river.

oneOf.description: The area everyone's map is held inside, or null until the Umpire sets it.

labelLanguage.description: Place names' language: an ISO 639-1 code, or "local".

hexSize.description: The hex grid's hexes, in metres across the flats (4828: 3 miles).

id.description: The membership's ID (used to remove a Player).

oneOf.description: The army they command, or null.
The Umpire, or null if the campaign has none (their account was deleted).
The caller's role, or null for an Admin who isn't a member.

CampaignRole.description: A campaign role (stored as its name).

CampaignStage.description: Where a campaign is: setting up (turn 0), or running (turn 1 or later is open).

umpireName.description: The Umpire's name, or null if it has none.

CampaignSummary.description: A campaign in the "my campaigns" list.

openTurn.description: The open turn's number (0 while setting up).

turns.description: Every turn so far, oldest first.

startProblems.description: For the Umpire: what stops the campaign starting (while setting up) or the next turn (once running).

closedAt.description: When the next opened (UTC), or null while it's the open turn.

submitted.description: How many armies have submitted (or completed) it.

armies.description: How many armies take part in it.

armyTurns.description: Each army's part: all of them for the Umpire, a commander's own for them.

oneOf.description: Its time of day (step 45); null for turn 0, the setup.

date.description: Its day, or null for the setup or a campaign without a start date.

CapitalStatus.description: Whether a town or city is a capital (it scores more).

ChangeEmailRequest.description:
Changes the email the account signs in with. Other sessions are signed out, and a notice goes
to the old address.

ChangePasswordRequest.description: Changes the password. Other sessions are signed out; this one continues.

commanderMemberId.description: A Player to command it (their membership ID), or null.

sideId.description: Its side: one of the campaign's two.

oneOf.description: Its colour, or null for the first one no other army has.
The nation it fights for (its flag), or null for none (a plain flag).

factionIds.description: The library factions it takes its units from, or null for none yet.

CreateArmyRequest.description: Adds an army to the campaign (at most 8).

CreateCampaignRequest.description: Starts a campaign; the caller becomes its Umpire.

armyId.description: Its army: only its units draw supply from it.

kind.description: Main, or intermediate (supplied from a main one, stocked for 15 turns).

cutOffTurns.description: An intermediate depot's turns in a row cut off from a main one.

DetailRelief.description: The lie of the land inside a hex, as its actual terrain finds it (the rules, p. 57).

DistanceUnit.description: How distances are shown (they're stored in metres).

DominantFeature.description: A hex's dominant feature, from the white die (the rules, p. 57).

EdgeSide.description:
A hex side an edge is stored on: N, NE or SE. The other three (S, SW, NW) are the neighbours'
N, NE and SE, so every edge has one place.

nation.description: Whose flag it shows (None: a plain one).

FactionResponse.description: A faction in the library, with its units.

nation.description: Whose flag it shows (None: a plain one).

FactionSummary.description: A faction in the library, as the list shows it.

Favorability.description:
How the ground favours the army that asked, from the green die: rolled only when both sides
come onto a battlefield together (the rules, p. 57).

ForgotPasswordRequest.description: Asks for a password reset link by email.

kind.description: Move (along the path) or Hold (stay where it is).

path.description:
A Move's steps: the hexes it passes through in order, from next to the unit's hex to where it
ends. Adjacent, inside the grid, and within what the unit can move in a turn.

forceMarch.description:
A Move by force march (decision 0018): a flat hex's worth further, in a Morning or Afternoon
turn only.

GiveOrderRequest.description: A unit's order for the turn.

Ground.description:
The movement table's columns: the ground a step is on (the rules, §E.1). Boats have the last
three; everyone else the first six.

Hex.description: A hex in a campaign's grid, by its axial coordinates (q east, r south-east).

setByUmpire.description: Set by the Umpire, so inference leaves it alone.

HexCellResponse.description: A hex with terrain on it.

favorability.description: How the ground favours the army that asked.

oneOf.description: The dice, or null if the Umpire set it.

forArmyId.description: The army that asked (the Umpire only sees it; null for others).

shownToArmyIds.description: The armies it's shown to (the Umpire only; empty for others).

red.description: The red die, after its modifier (0–7).

green.description: The green die, if favourability was rolled.

side.description: The hex's side the edge is on: N, NE or SE (the others are its neighbours').

river.description: Whether a river lies along it, between the hexes.

bridge.description: Whether a bridge crosses the river.

waterway.description: A navigable course across it, and which way it flows.

setByUmpire.description: Set by the Umpire, so inference leaves it alone.

HexEdgeResponse.description: An edge with a road, river or waterway on it.

HexFeatures.description: What's in a hex, by the rule book's table (p. 57).

size.description: A town or city, or none.

walled.description: The town or city is walled (only with one).

fortress.description: A fortress, in the town or city or on its own.

capital.description: Whether the town or city is a capital (only with one).

name.description: Its name, if given (only with a town, city or fortress).

HexSettlement.description: A hex's town, city or fortress (decision 0016).

side.description: The hex's side: N, NE or SE.

river.description: Whether a river lies along it, between the hexes.

bridge.description: Whether a bridge crosses the river (only with a river).

waterway.description: A navigable course across it, and which way it flows.

InferredHexEdge.description: An edge's inferred road, river and waterway.

myRole.description: The caller's role: Player, or their existing role if already a member.

JoinCampaignResponse.description: The campaign the caller is now in.

joinCode.description: The code, safe to use in a URL as it is.

JoinCodeResponse.description: A campaign's join code. The app builds the join link from it.

umpireName.description: The Umpire's name, or null if the campaign has none.

JoinPreviewResponse.description: What a join link shows before joining. Public: anyone with the code can see it.

LoginRequest.description: Sign in with email and password.

east.description: The eastern edge's longitude (east of West: bounds can't cross 180°).

north.description: The northern edge's latitude (north of South).

MapBounds.description: The area a campaign's map is held inside, in degrees (west to east, south to north).

water.description: Rivers, canals, lakes and the sea.

MapLayers.description: Which of the map's layers are shown.

endsAt.description: When it ends on its own (UTC).

MasqueradeInfo.description: A masquerade: an Admin using the app as the signed-in user.

nation.description: The nation it fights for, drawn as its flag.

email.description: Their email, which is also what they sign in with.

isManager.description: Whether they're a Manager: they edit the library (decision 0015).

oneOf.description: When an Admin is using the app as this user (decision 0012): who, and until when. Null otherwise.

MovementClass.description: The rule book's movement classes (section XII.E; decision 0014).

hexes.description: Hexes a turn, in halves; 0 if the class can't cross it.

MovementRateDto.description: One cell of the movement table.

rates.description: Every class on each of its grounds.

rules.description: Whether it's the rule book's table, unchanged.

Nation.description:
The nation or state of the Napoleonic wars an army fights for. The front-end draws its flag (a
simplified one) as the army's icon; None is a plain flag in the army's colour. Stored by name.

OrderKind.description: What a unit does in a turn.

items.description: This page's items, in a stable order.

pageSize.description: The requested page size (the last page can have fewer items).

totalCount.description: How many items there are across all pages.

PagedResponseOfAdminCampaignSummary.description: One page of a list that can grow large.

items.description: This page's items, in a stable order.

pageSize.description: The requested page size (the last page can have fewer items).

totalCount.description: How many items there are across all pages.

PagedResponseOfCampaignSummary.description: One page of a list that can grow large.

items.description: This page's items, in a stable order.

pageSize.description: The requested page size (the last page can have fewer items).

totalCount.description: How many items there are across all pages.

PagedResponseOfUserSummary.description: One page of a list that can grow large.

description.description: Its name with where it is ("Leipzig, Saxony, Germany").

oneOf.description: Its extent, if the service knows it.

PlaceResult.description: A place found by a search, to frame the map on.

PlaceUnitRequest.description: Where the Umpire places a unit: a hex in the campaign's grid.

turn.description: The turn it belongs to: the one attrition closed, or the one open at an edit.

note.description: What it was for ("Forced march, ×2"), if anything.

byName.description: Who made it; null if their account has since been deleted.

PointsChangeResponse.description: A change to a unit's points (decision 0018).

RegisterRequest.description: Sign up. The account is signed in straight away.

name.description: The side's new name, unique in the campaign.

ResetPasswordRequest.description: Sets a new password with the code from a reset link.

note.description: A note on the turn as a whole.

unitNotes.description: Notes on units in the army, at most one each.

ReviewTurnRequest.description: Why the Umpire sends a turn back or reverts it: a note, and notes on units.

RoadQuality.description: The best road across an edge.

forArmyId.description: The army that asked, if any.

favorability.description: Roll the green die too: both sides have come onto the field together.

flatMinusOne.description: Take one off the red die (a flat hex only, at the Umpire's choice).

RollHexDetailRequest.description: The Umpire shakes the dice for a hex (again: the new roll replaces the old).

cells.description: The hexes, each once, inside the grid.

edges.description: The edges, each once, touching the grid.

SaveCampaignGridRequest.description:
The terrain inferred for the whole grid. It replaces what inference saved before; what the
Umpire set stays. Hexes and edges with nothing on them can be left out.

q.description: The hex (axial q), inside the campaign's grid.

SaveDepotRequest.description: The Umpire places, moves or changes a depot.

nation.description: Whose flag it shows (None: a plain one).

SaveFactionRequest.description: Adds a faction to the library, or changes one.

rates.description: Every class on each of its grounds.

SaveMovementTableRequest.description:
The Umpire's movement table: every class on each of its grounds, once (land units on the six
land grounds, boats on the three water ones).

type.description: What kind of troops it is.

SaveUnitRequest.description: Adds a unit to a faction in the library, or changes one.

SetManagerRequest.description: Makes a user a Manager (decision 0015), or not.

SettlementSize.description: The town or city in a hex, if any (decision 0016): the map legend's small and large cities.

userId.description: The new Umpire: a Player in the campaign, or any other user.

SetUmpireRequest.description: Makes a user the campaign's Umpire.

armyCount.description: How many armies are in it.

SideResponse.description: A side in the campaign. Every member sees them all.

attrition.description:
The attrition the closing turn cost, as the Umpire confirmed it: a loss for each unit that owes
one (see the attrition list), and no other.

Terrain.description: A hex's ground (decision 0014): what it costs to move into it.

accessToken.description: The bearer token for API calls.

expiresIn.description: Seconds until the access token expires; refresh before then.

TokenResponse.description:
A signed-in session. The access token goes in `Authorization: Bearer …`; the refresh
token is never in a body: it's set as an HttpOnly cookie that only /api/auth receives.

movesInRow.description: Moving turns in its run, before its first forced march is made.

forcedMarchTurns.description: Turns of forced march it has still to rest off (a Hold each).

moveCosts.description: The attrition moving this turn would cost, as a multiple of the rules' scale (0: none).

forceMarchCosts.description: The same for a force march.

orderCosts.description: The same for its order this turn as given (0 with none: a rest).

UnitMarchResponse.description: A unit's forced marches as the open turn began (decision 0018).

UnitNoteDto.description: The Umpire's note on one unit's order.

turn.description: The turn this is its position after.

status.description: That army turn's status (a Draft's positions are orders not yet approved).

kind.description: Its order: Move (or placed, in turn 0) or Hold.

path.description: A Move's steps, the hexes it passes through in order; empty otherwise.

byUmpire.description: Whether the Umpire set this order, on the commander's behalf.

progress.description:
Part of the way (0–1) into the path's last hex, which takes more than a turn: the unit is still
in Q, R. Null when it got where it was going.

forceMarch.description: Whether the move is a force march (decision 0018).

UnitPosition.description: Where a unit is (or is ordered to be) after a turn.

type.description: What kind of troops it is.

UnitType.description:
What kind of troops a unit is (stored as its name), grouped by the rule book's movement
classes (decision 0014): infantry and foot artillery; light infantry and partisans; light
cavalry and scouts; medium and heavy cavalry and horse artillery; supply and siege artillery;
and boats, which keep to waterways and lakes (decision 0016).

sideId.description: Its side: one of the campaign's two.

color.description: Its colour. Two armies can share one.

nation.description: The nation it fights for, drawn as its flag.

factionIds.description:
The library factions it takes its units from (one it has units from can't be dropped), or null
to leave them as they are.

UpdateArmyRequest.description: Changes an army's name, side, colour, nation and factions.

type.description: What kind of troops it is.

UpdateArmyUnitRequest.description: Changes the campaign's copy of a unit (the library's stays as it is).

startDate.description: The first turn's day, or null for none.

firstTurnPart.description: The first turn's time of day.

morningNations.description: Whose infantry move a flat hex further each Morning.

afternoonNations.description: Whose infantry move a flat hex less each Afternoon.

UpdateCampaignCalendarRequest.description: The Umpire sets the campaign's calendar.

infantryTypes.description: The unit types counted towards the infantry limit.

cavalryTypes.description: The unit types counted towards the cavalry limit (none in both).

infantryLimit.description: The most points of infantry a side may have in a hex.

cavalryLimit.description: The most points of cavalry a side may have in a hex.

UpdateCampaignConcentrationRequest.description: The Umpire sets the campaign's concentration settings.

oneOf.description: The area everyone's map is held inside, or null for none yet.

labelLanguage.description: Place names' language: an ISO 639-1 code from the list, or "local".

hexSize.description:
The hex grid's hexes, in metres across the flats. With the bounds, fixed once the campaign has
started.

UpdateCampaignMapRequest.description: Changes a campaign's map settings (all of them).

UpdateCampaignRequest.description: Changes a campaign's name and description.

UpdateHexCellRequest.description: The Umpire sets a hex's terrain.

favorability.description: How the ground favours the army that asked.

forArmyId.description: The army that asked, if any.

UpdateHexDetailRequest.description: The Umpire sets a hex's actual terrain, and who sees it.

river.description: Whether a river lies along it, between the hexes.

bridge.description: Whether a bridge crosses the river (only with a river).

waterway.description: A navigable course across it, and which way it flows.

UpdateHexEdgeRequest.description: The Umpire sets an edge's road, river and waterway.

UserCampaign.description: A campaign a user is in.

email.description: Their email (what they sign in with).

isManager.description: Whether they're a Manager: they edit the library (decision 0015).

lockedOutUntil.description: When a sign-in lockout ends (UTC), if they're locked out now.

campaigns.description: The campaigns they're in, with their role, sorted by name.

UserDetails.description: One user, for admins, with the campaigns they're in.

email.description: Their email (what they sign in with).

isManager.description: Whether they're a Manager: they edit the library (decision 0015).

UserSummary.description: A user in the admin user list.

Waterway.description:
A navigable course across an edge (decision 0016), for boats: which way it flows, out of the
hex the edge is stored on and into the one across, or back in.

Bearer.description: The accessToken from register, login or refresh.
